intro.title: Hello, I'm Lain
intro.desc:
Robotics developer.
Currently interning at a humanoid robotics company.
Focused on MCU and Linux application development, motion control, RL deployment, and robot perception.

item0.title: Qianxing Intelligence Humanoid Robots
item0.desc: Core motion-control contributor for multiple humanoid platforms, responsible for motion-data processing and hardware debugging. Built a frame-by-frame IK retargeting method for low-latency BVH-to-robot whole-body teleoperation, trained low-level motion and high-level decision policies in mjlab as a hierarchical dual-network controller, and created a URDF-driven self-occlusion mask pipeline to reduce robot-body interference in vision detection.

item1.title: LocoWiki Robot Locomotion Resource Hub
item1.desc: A one-stop robot-locomotion community for ROBOCON preparation, research, and engineering reference. It curates competition rules, university technical talks, paper reading lists, and mainstream open-source projects, and has grown to 120,000+ views and 1,100+ members.

item2.title: HighTorque Mini Open-Source Quadruped
item2.desc: Led a mini open-source quadruped project during my internship at HighTorque, establishing the development workflow and moving modules from prototype validation toward productization. Trained locomotion policies with HIMLoco, handled sim-to-real deployment and gap adaptation, reproduced DreamWaQ, walk-these-ways, and staged-reward strategies, and wrote debugging and user guides.

item3.title: ROBOCON Parallel Force-Control Robot
item3.desc: Led modeling and motion-control development for an 8-DOF parallel quadruped, designed foot trajectories, and validated VMC in Webots. Deployed FAST-LIO mapping and AMCL + move_base navigation for autonomous movement in structured environments. Led the team to three National Second Prizes in the 2025 ROBOCON bionic-legged Speed, Obstacle, and Cross-Country events; the project also received provincial innovation-program funding.

item4.title: Bionic Lobster Submersible
item4.desc: Developed the control and embedded systems for a buoyancy-adjustable multi-DOF lobster-inspired underwater robot, unifying stepper peristaltic pump, motor, and servo actuation with IMU acquisition. Built a vectored-thrust model for its irregular multi-thruster layout to achieve omnidirectional control. Won the 2024 Fujian provincial Grand Prize and was covered by Xinhua News Agency and Guangming Daily.

item5.title: Intelligent Rice Transplanting and Harvesting Robot
item5.desc: FreeRTOS-based agricultural robot for rice transplanting and harvesting. Controlled DJI 3508 motors for gripper lifting and an omnidirectional chassis, achieving ±5 mm positioning accuracy. Participated in pneumatic design and hardware wiring, supporting dual-robot collaboration.

item6.title: SliverWolf Desktop Quadruped and Arm
item6.desc: An open-source desktop 12-DOF serial-link quadruped with an optional robotic arm and gripper. Built around STM32F103 and MG92R micro servos, the repository includes body and arm STL files, PCB PDFs, quadruped firmware, voice relay firmware, posture/button-control examples, and an LD3320 voice-recognition project. Serial commands cover standing, forward/backward walking, turning, strafing, crawling, handshaking, light effects, and one-click object fetching through Bluetooth, IMU/button, and voice-control paths.

item7.title: 3508 Legged-Robot Drive Test Platform
item7.desc: A DJI M3508-powered quadruped drive validation platform iterated by the MTI Robotics Team at Fujian University of Technology since 2022. Starting from an F427 ROBOCON chassis architecture, it evolved into a quadruped control program with RC/keyboard operation, variable PID motor parameters, stable standing, gyroscope attitude balance, LiDAR height holding, gait timing, frame compensation, backward gait, turning, and track testing for multiple ROBOCON legged-robot seasons.

item8.title: ROBOCON2024-PPS
item8.desc: MTIPPS is a planar base-axis positioning system for ROBOCON 2024 robots. Based on STM32F103C8T6, RS485 absolute encoders, and omni-wheel code disks, it reads XY displacement with millimeter-level travel recording while collecting Hi219 gyroscope attitude data. The system streams positioning and attitude information to the robot mainboard for chassis localization, path-planning, and autonomous driving tests.

item9.title: ArenaX Robotics Terrain & Policy Validation Environment
item9.desc: A MuJoCo procedural terrain and scene tool for robot-policy validation. Its bilingual PyQt editor generates flat, sloped, stair, noise, and mixed-obstacle terrains and exports MuJoCo XML, heightmaps, and JSON metadata. The embedded MuJoCo simulation page supports interactive testing of M20 and Go2 robots with ONNX locomotion policies, plus external terrain-library loading.

item10.title: S-Dog Quadruped Robot
item10.desc: Developing a 12-DOF quadruped and contributing to lightweight mechanical design and system integration. The 10.25 kg robot carries up to 5 kg. Reworked proprioceptive observations, action space, and rewards with reference to RoboGauge, and added AMP to learn motion priors from mocap data. Deployed obstacle-crossing, platform-climbing, and self-recovery policies on hardware: 20 cm obstacles and 40 cm platforms. Exhibited at WAIC 2026.

item11.title: G-Exo Consumer 4-DOF Active Lower-Limb Exoskeleton
item11.desc: Led development of a consumer-grade four-DOF active lower-limb exoskeleton, owning mechanical and electronics design, URDF modeling, and system architecture. Co-developed a MyoSuite + MuJoCo + PPO training pipeline using a TCN to encode IMU and joint time-series features and output assistive torque. Won the alloop track at the inaugural Physical AI Hackathon and HKD 30,000.

item0.title: Robotics Engineer Learning Roadmap (Preview) - Lain-Ego on Zhihu
item0.desc: A structured learning path for robotics engineers, covering core areas such as motion control, perception, embedded systems, and SLAM, with phased study suggestions and resource indexing.

item1.title: A Guide to Career Paths in the Robotics Industry — for High School Students - KKR Database on Zhihu
item1.desc: An overview of development paths and subfields in the robotics industry for high school students, helping connect university major choices with career directions through a clear industry landscape.

item2.title: On the Organizational Maturity of University Robotics Competition Teams - KKR Database on Zhihu
item2.desc: Exploring how university robotics competition teams can improve organizational efficiency, knowledge transfer, and collaboration — from team structure and document management to sustainable season planning.
